newsitem.title: FRANCE: French offer 16,000 tonnes barley to intervention.
newsitem.headline: French offer 16,000 tonnes barley to intervention.

text.p: Some 16,000 tonnes of barley were offered into French intervention before the May 31 deadline, France's grain office ONIC said on Monday.
The last-minute offers placed on Saturday were processed by ONIC's regional offices of Chalon sur Marne and Dijon in eastern France and will take a few days to be approved, an ONIC official said.
Despite the offers -- the only ones made in the entire November-to-May intervention buying-in season -- EU-controlled intervention will remain almost empty in France this year.

France had ended the 1995/96 season with 11,000 tonnes of soft wheat and 1,000 tonnes of barley in intervention stocks, ONIC data shows. Those tonnages however resulted from carryover stocks from the 1994/95 season as farmers had sold no grain into intervention in the 1995/96 season when global markets were tight.
Despite more ample supplies in the past 12 months, intervention offers had been widely expected to be low again this year.
Uncertainty over the new crop following nearly four months of drought have kept domestic prices in most regions above intervention prices, even though May rainfall was above normal.
